originalTitle: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq end higher on cool inflation data, solid bank earnings
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the US stock market today: the S&P 500 and Nasdaq went up because of some good news about inflation and bank earnings. Inflation, which is the rate at which prices are rising, was lower than expected in June, which is a good sign. Also, some big banks like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs reported strong earnings, which made investors happy. This good news made investors less worried about the Federal Reserve raising interest rates soon, which is why the stock market went up, even though there are some tensions in the Middle East. Overall, it was a positive day for the stock market, except for a few companies like IBM that had some disappointing news.

originalTitle: US derivatives regulator blocks Kalshi from canceling Michigan trades despite court order
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: a company called Kalshi had some trades in the state of Michigan that a court said they had to cancel. But the US regulator in charge of derivatives (which are a type of investment) is not letting them cancel those trades. This is causing tension between the federal government and the state of Michigan, which has its own rules about gambling. The regulator's decision is important because it affects how prediction markets (where people bet on the outcome of events) will be regulated in the future. This conflict raises questions about who gets to make the rules and how it will impact companies like Kalshi.

originalTitle: Why IBM shares crashed 26%: CEO Arvind Krishna highlights customer spending shifts towards AI
simplifiedContent: IBM's stock price dropped by 26% because the company's recent performance was not as good as expected. The main reason for this is that customers are changing how they spend their money, and they are now focusing more on artificial intelligence (AI). IBM's CEO, Arvind Krishna, said that customers are prioritizing AI and trying to get the necessary hardware, but the company had some problems with execution and its mainframe business. This change in customer spending and the company's own mistakes led to a big drop in the stock price. The drop in stock price is significant and unusual for IBM, indicating a major impact on investor confidence.

originalTitle: Multibagger Signature Global shares to be in focus on Wednesday after Q1 pre-sales rise 25% QoQ
simplifiedContent: Signature Global, a company listed on the stock market, will be closely watched on Wednesday due to its recent sales performance. The company's sales for the first quarter of the financial year 2027 were ₹1,970 crore, which is 25% lower than the same time last year. However, sales increased by 25% compared to the previous quarter, thanks in part to the launch of a new project called Tonino Lamborghini Residences. This increase in sales from the previous quarter is a positive sign for the company. The company's shares may be affected by this news, making them worth paying attention to on Wednesday.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver rebound as softer US inflation eases Fed rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: The prices of gold and silver went up on July 14th because the rate of inflation in the US was lower than expected. This decrease in inflation makes it less likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates, which is good news for gold and silver investors. As a result, the price of gold futures rose to $4,112 and the price of silver rose to $60. This increase in price is also happening at a time when there are rising tensions in the Middle East, which can also affect the prices of gold and silver. The lower inflation rate and other factors combined to make gold and silver more attractive to investors, causing their prices to go up.

originalTitle: Govt reviews fresh bids for IDBI Bank as stake sale process gathers pace
simplifiedContent: The Indian government and a company called LIC are trying to sell a big part of a bank called IDBI Bank. They want to sell almost 61% of the bank, which is currently owned by them, and also let someone else take control of how the bank is run. The government owns about 30% of the bank, and LIC owns about 30% as well. This is a big deal because together, they own almost 95% of the bank, so selling this stake will be a significant change. The process of finding a buyer for the bank's stake is moving forward as the government reviews new bids.
